brief: Distinguish borrowed money from earned income and identify the future repayment obligation created by using credit.

en-US.scenario: Fictional US-dollar examples for "Borrowing creates an obligation"; illustrative amounts, not current prices or product offers. No assumption of salary, bank ownership or spare income.

es-MX.scenario: Ejemplos ficticios en pesos mexicanos para "Pedir prestado crea una obligación"; montos ilustrativos, no precios vigentes ni ofertas. No se supone nómina, cuenta bancaria ni dinero sobrante.

pt-BR.scenario: Exemplos fictícios em reais para "Pegar emprestado cria obrigação"; valores ilustrativos, não preços atuais nem ofertas. Sem supor salário, conta bancária ou dinheiro sobrando.

objective.observable_action: Distinguish borrowed money from earned income and identify the future repayment obligation created by using credit.
objective.success_criterion: Complete the fresh-context transfer using only its visible information.

instruction.relevance: Borrowing can make money available now, but creates a payment obligation later. Keep both sides in the plan.
instruction.misconception: Treating an available credit limit or borrowed deposit as extra income with no future claim on resources.
instruction.numeracy_support: Use money direction and future payment dates; this lesson introduces the obligation before interest calculations.

evidence.reasoning: Ana receives a loan of 100. Her usable money rises by 100, but she also owes repayment under the agreement.
A credit limit states how much may be borrowed. Using it creates debt; it is not earned income.
The receipt and the repayment obligation exist together.
Credit availability describes borrowing capacity, not income.
A useful purchase still leaves its financing obligation.
Receiving money can mean different things depending on its source and terms.
The future obligation cannot be planned without its terms.
Receiving the item now does not remove the later payment commitments.

delayed_retrieval.fresh_context: Apply this skill in a later integrated decision with a different constraint.
